subject: BluePeak Therapeutics — questions on data handling, subprocessors, and opt-out flow
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@bluepeak.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: counsel@bluepeak-legal.com, security@bluepeak.com
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarifications on data handling and opt-out

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed by the latency and the canary features. Before we proceed to procurement, a couple of compliance items came up from legal/security that we need clarified in writing:

- We need an explicit, signed commitment that BluePeak customer data will not be used to improve or retrain any Redwood models unless we opt in (no-training by default). Is that something you can commit to in the DPA or an addendum?
- A list of subprocessors that may have access to request/response data (and the locations where those subprocessors operate).
- Cross-border transfer details: what safeguards apply for EU-origin data routed through US-based GPUs?
- Is there a self-service opt-out for model-improvement processing for specific prompt sets or users? If so, how is it enforced in the runtime (e.g., headers, customer-scoped flags)?

Attachments requested by our security team: SOC 2 snapshot and a CSV template for subprocessors if you can populate it.

Can you please route this to the right person on your side and provide a draft wording or redline for the no-training clause?

Best,
Anya
Director, AI Safety & Compliance
BluePeak Therapeutics

---
Attachment: SOC2-Request-Template.txt (referenced, not attached)
From: neha.kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@bluepeak.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on data handling and opt-out

Hi Anya — appreciate the follow-up and the clear list. Looping in Dev (legal) and Marissa (account lead) so we can respond with formal wording and ops details.

Quick answers while we draft:
- Redwood can commit to a default "no-model-improvement" posture for requests made to a customer-designated endpoint or tenant: data routed to that endpoint will not be incorporated into model training or shared with model improvement pipelines. We typically capture this via tenant config + request flags.
- I'll share our current subprocessors registry and our standard DPA redline.
- For cross-border transfers, we rely on SCCs where applicable and customer-region routing; I will include the technical routing doc.
- Opt-out can be implemented as a per-tenant feature (disabled by default for the public API), and we can add header-level enforcement (x-redwood-no-train: true) plus audit logs.

Expect a draft by EOD. If BluePeak prefers a separate addendum versus altering the DPA text, we can do either — happy to mirror your procurement preference.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Note: attaching a link to our standard DPA in the next email.
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BluePeak — suggested no-training / opt-out language

Neha / Marissa — draft language below that I recommend including in a short addendum to the DPA (keeps core DPA stable). Feel free to send to BluePeak with track changes: 

---- Suggested addendum text (for legal review) ----
1) No-Model-Improvement Commitment: Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, or derived artifacts) to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any Redwood models or model weights, whether internally or via third parties, unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in for specific datasets and time periods.

2) Operational Enforcement: Requests made via Customer's dedicated tenant or via API requests containing the header 'x-redwood-no-train: true' will be flagged at the service edge and routed to an execution path that prevents logging to model-improvement pipelines. Audit logs will record the header and enforcement decision.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and their processing locations within 5 business days of execution of the DPA, and will notify Customer 30 days prior to adding any subprocessors that will access request/response content.

4) Cross-border Transfers: Data transfers outside the EEA shall be protected by appropriate safeguards (e.g., SCCs) and by routing controls allowing Customer to designate region-only processing where available; Redwood will document the fallback behavior if region-only capacity is not available.

---- end text ----

I also attached a CSV template of subprocessors and a copy of our SOC2 report excerpt for context (redacted). I recommend we prepare a short ops note describing enforcement points (edge flag, tenant config, KV cache handling).

Dev Patel
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: subprocessors.csv; SOC2-Report-2024.pdf
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@bluepeak.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BluePeak Therapeutics — questions on data handling, subprocessors, and opt-out flow

Anya — thanks for the questions. To keep procurement moving, we can do the following:

1) Send the DPA with Dev's addendum language as a tracked change (attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf).
2) Provide populated subprocessors.csv (attached) and a short summary table of which subprocessors see decrypted content vs. metadata only.
3) Offer an ops-oriented runbook: how to set the tenant and header for no-train, and how BluePeak can verify via audit logs. We can run a short tech call with your SRE/security folks to show the enforcement and logging.

If that sounds good, I'll request our legal ops to create the DocuSign envelope and target a 3-business-day turnaround for review.

PS — for the opt-out granularity: we usually support tenant-level or API-key-level opt-outs; per-prompt opt-outs are possible but expensive to operate and test. Happy to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf
From: counsel@bluepeak-legal.com <counsel@bluepeak-legal.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: anya.patel@bluepeak.com, security@bluepeak.com
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BluePeak Therapeutics — questions on data handling, subprocessors, and opt-out flow

Marissa / Neha,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the addendum language — appreciate the clarity. A few editorial redlines from legal/security: 

- We propose tightening 1) to explicitly include "derived embeddings" and "diagnostic metadata" in the definition of Customer Data that is covered by the no-improvement commitment.
- For 3) subprocessors: please confirm whether any cloud managed services (e.g., logging as a service, analytics) will receive plaintext responses. In our redline we ask that any subprocessors with access to plaintext be limited to those listed in the CSV and subject to written notice and an approval window.
- For 4) transfers: request that Redwood add an SLA for routing to region-designated capacity where available (e.g., 99% of requests processed in-designated-region when capacity is available).

Can you also provide a short sample audit log entry that shows the x-redwood-no-train header and enforcement flag? That will help our InfoSec team validate.

We will review the DPA PDF and upload redlines to the DocuSign envelope (please send link).

Regards,
M. Jansen
Counsel, BluePeak Therapeutics

Operational notes: prioritize providing the sample audit log (anonymized) and the populated CSV today so Marissa can load the DocuSign envelope. Avoid committing to per-prompt opt-out SLAs at this stage.

Laura Bennett
